newsitem.title: USA: USDA reviews foreign meat inspection equivalence.
newsitem.headline: USDA reviews foreign meat inspection equivalence.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Wednesday began the process of determining which foreign meat inspection systems would be considered equivalent to new U.S. inspection rules.
Under the World Trade Organization rules, the U.S. can require foreign meat be inspected under standards equivalent to U.S. laws before allowing it to enter the country.

"We are committed to developing our policy for applying the concept of equivalence in an open, transparent and participatory fashion," USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service deputy administrator John Prucha said.
Prucha was speaking at the start of a two-day public hearing on foreign equivalence, attended by representatives from Australia, Canada, the European Union and other exporters.
Prucha said he anticipated recieving proposals for alternative inspection systems from countries that wanted to continue exporting to the United States soon.
USDA announced an overhaul of its meat and poultry inspection earlier this year, which will introduce so-called Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) principles over three years.
